The residue order is preserved, but the character itself is changed in the saved alignment.

note: Q8 part 2 verdict: the codon aligner path never loses or reorders residues. The fast engine strips only gap characters at the boundary (workspace seq replace at codon-align-worker.js:11), stores the scoring copy separately from the original letters (codon-align.js:449), and rebuilds each result row from the original letters, so case, U and any '*' below the photo-refusal thresholds (codon-align.js:81 NT_OK) survive intact in order; '!' frameshift padding is by design (timeout guard unless opts.frameRestored). MACSE, by contrast, either aborts on '*' (macse-align.js:105/109) or silently rewrites letters unknown to its table — e.g. U and IUPAC codes — to 'N' in the result rows (SeqNT constructor + checkNT), which is the only true defect found (medium; every letter stays in order but characters are altered). I did NOT verify the MACSE N2B table contents directly, so confidence 3. The 26188/26189 guard placement question is confirmed with grep-verified quotes: the codon branch returns at 26188, the guard runs at 26189 only afterward (and _alignerRestoreResidues at 26212 is MAFFT-branch only), so the codon path is unguarded; this is by design since MACSE would error rather than silently change data. Items 7 and to a lesser extent 2 and 1 carry confidence caveats; see the 8th item. No further reading was needed beyond the final verification greps.
